The nucleus ambiguus serves both the muscles of the throat and the heart and lungs; that the two roles share one nucleus does not mean that each of its nerve cells serves both.

The raphe nuclei of the medulla and their groups of cells differ from one another, and the dorsal raphe nucleus is a separate structure, higher up, in the midbrain.

sources.citation: Naidich et al. (2004), human insula, dissection and 1.5 T MRI
sources.evidence_type: primary human cadaver anatomy and 1.5 T MRI
sources.scope_and_limit: The frontoparietal opercular tissue sits above and covers the upper face of the insula. A labelled specimen and MRI show postcentral and supramarginal cortex along the overlying tissue, near Heschl’s gyrus. Gross neighbourhood and orientation only. These specimens and images were acquired independently of the Allen label. No landmark error in mm follows without a validated cross-specimen transform.

sources.citation: Eickhoff et al. (2006), human parietal operculum, stereotaxic anatomy
sources.evidence_type: primary human postmortem histology and probabilistic mapping
sources.scope_and_limit: The cortex turns inward along the upper bank of the lateral sulcus. The coronal views place parietal opercular cortex above the Sylvian fissure, lateral to the circular sulcus of the insula. Microscopic analysis separates OP1–OP4. Reference view and relative location. The OP fields are a different parcellation and are unavailable as separate voxels in label 13230.

sources.citation: Eickhoff et al. (2007), human opercular responses to touch
sources.scope_and_limit: The researchers found body-part-related responses in two lateral parietal-opercular fields. Different fields within this gross part of the brain can respond differently. Task-related indirect signal in other participants. The atlas surface supplies no BOLD values, functional border, connection or clinical information.
